title: Normalize API Users
prompt: A TypeScript frontend receives snake_case user objects from an API but the app uses camelCase. Write a function that maps each API user to { id, displayName, isActive }.

explanation.beginner:
Example: normalizeApiUsers([{"id":"1","display_name":"Ada","is_active":true}]) produces [{"id":"1","displayName":"Ada","isActive":true}]. The result must follow this precise rule: A TypeScript frontend receives snake_case user objects from an API but the app uses camelCase. Write a function that maps each API user to { id, displayName, isActive }. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “handles multiple users”: input [[{"id":"1","display_name":"Ada","is_active":true},{"id":"2","display_name":"Grace","is_active":false}]] produces [{"id":"1","displayName":"Ada","isActive":true},{"id":"2","displayName":"Grace","isActive":false}]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
